# Buzz recipe — turn a locked short into a reviewable hosted source candidate

Apply this to a different short; do not copy S83's story, source choices or scene design.

    #build #shortform
    Claim exactly one unclaimed short. Read its canonical script, fact ledger, word timing and current voice receipts. Freeze the script and narration by path and text hash. Check the receipts for exact duration, complete ASR, isolated names, pace and speaker identity; record each mismatch as open. Search for existing visuals by story ID before authoring. Build three distinct concepts, choose one with a specific story reason, then write scene beats directly against canonical word times. Every evidence object must name a verified source and show its date; no invented UI, quote, statistic or mark. Capture real source pages/logos only on the verified public Ubuntu repository. Pin the parent commit and helper blobs, hash-bound inputs and exact output allowlist. Run the hosted source capture once; inspect every PNG, every seam, every caption and the closing CTA against P1. Return the strongest remaining defect with timestamp and concrete correction. The maker does not approve.

## Fixes applied to this candidate

- A source-backed metric replaces the draft's invented-looking 3:59 stopwatch value: the frame reads “less than 4 minutes per patient,” matching the trust's actual statement.
- The visual metaphor is a single clinical note that turns over at the BBC correction; the measured task and unpublished waiting-time evidence then occupy separate fields.
- The six-minute report is labelled as BBC reporting about Dr Jamil Aslam, and the eight-month pilot/two-trust detail is separated into the trust's source.
- The caption band is reserved below all source objects; captions are derived deterministically from the locked S83 word-timing JSON.

## Independent validation required

The maker can check only text, provenance and structure. A different reviewer must authenticate the real publisher page/mark and portrait, view all hosted frames in sequence, inspect each seam at −40/+20/+60 ms, confirm source text and captured crop are legible at portrait scale, verify no source image/text collides with captions, and compare the hook, weakest beat and signature against P1. An ears-capable reviewer must hear the selected voice and verify “Heidi,” the clinicians' plural, pacing, pauses, and final mux. Record maker/hash, hosted run ID and branch, observed frames, one defect/fix cycle, reviewer identity, Eagle result, remaining limitations and exact next step. A distributed recipe is teaching only; demonstrated learning requires a later distinct short whose hosted review shows Buzz applied it without root rewriting.
